title: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd - 500570 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Tata Motors PV FY26 volumes hit a record 6.42 lakh units (+15% YoY); JLR full-year EBIT only 0.7%, with Rs 4,100 Cr of exceptionals.
summary.overview: India PV business recovered strongly in H2 after a muted H1, with Q4 offtake above 2 lakh units (+37% YoY) and the company ranked number two on Vahan with over 14% share. Consolidated revenue for Q4 was about Rs 105,000 Cr (+7% YoY), with PBT before exceptionals of Rs 7,200 Cr, while full-year PBT of Rs 2,500 Cr excluded about Rs 4,100 Cr of exceptionals (cyber, labour code, demerger stamp duty). JLR delivered 95,000 Q4 wholesales and 9.2% EBIT, but full-year EBIT was 0.7% and management called the full-year performance far from intended. Management flagged commodity headwinds of 5-6% of revenue over 9-12 months and a Middle East demand hit in Q1, with guidance deferred to the June investor days.

segments.name: India PV (TMPV)
segments.commentary: FY26 volumes of 6.42 lakh units (+15%) with Q4 above 2 lakh units; EVs sold 92,000 (+43%) with over 40% share, and CNG at 27% of portfolio (over 1.7 lakh units). Exports were 10,000+ in FY26 with FY27 target of 70-100% growth.

segments.name: JLR
segments.commentary: Q4 wholesales 95,000 and EBIT 9.2%, but FY26 EBIT of 0.7% and cash outflow of about GBP 2.2 billion, with two production quarters lost to the cyber incident. Defender grew YoY in Q4; Jaguar volumes fell 5,700 units as the brand transitions.

guidance_outlook: JLR targets GBP 1.7 billion of cost savings over two years, aiming to bring cash breakeven volume back toward 300,000 units a year; savings to start showing from H2 FY27.
India: management expects industry growth of about 10% in FY27, with high double-digit growth in H1 and moderation in H2; TMPV aims for industry-beating growth.

India: about 0.5% price increase taken in April 2026, with further measured price increases under consideration; commodity headwind estimated at 5-6% of revenue over 9-12 months (about 3.5-4% expected in Q4 FY26).
JLR financial guidance for FY27 to be given at the Investor Day on 17 June 2026; India Analyst Day on 23 June 2026.
EV production to rise beyond 10,000 units a month from May 2026; Sierra.ev launch expected next quarter.
capex_capacity: India FY26 capex about Rs 4,300 Cr (7.5% of revenue), within guided range for combined PV and EV capex.
Sierra supply constrained by casting suppliers on the new engine; immediate milestone is to cross 10,000 units a month with additional suppliers added.
EV run rate about 24,000 a quarter on average and about 27,000 in Q4, with a monthly run rate of about 9,000; production to rise by about 10% from May.
JLR investment is largely in UK plant facilities for three new architectures and BEV powertrains at the Wolverhampton propulsion facility.
Dealer inventory in India about 20 days; waiting periods 4-8 weeks, longer for Sierra and certain EVs.
demand_pricing: India industry FY26 volumes hit a record 4.7 million units (+8%); H2 grew 17% post GST 2.0, and April-May demand momentum stayed at a high level.
Nexon and Punch ranked number one and number three models in the industry during H2 FY26.
EV bookings up roughly 25-30% after the Middle East crisis began in February, though supply, not demand, is the constraint.

JLR ASPs fell marginally QoQ to about GBP 72,000 from GBP 76,000, mainly due to sterling strength against the dollar ($1.36 Q4 average vs $1.325 in Q3). Q4 gross margin fell on higher VME (7% vs 5% last year) and warranty charges.
JLR China volumes fell 27% YoY in FY26 due to luxury tax and dealer-stock reduction; US retailer stock brought down after tariffs, now slightly below normal levels.
Middle East (6% of JLR sales mix) expected to be hit in Q1 FY27; Middle East dealers are running out of stock.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of the commodity headwind, and how will it be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated the impact at 5-6% of revenue over 9-12 months, with about 2% offset by cost reductions in FY26 and 0.5% price increase taken in April. Further measured price increases are under consideration but not decided.

qa_highlights.question: Will EV volumes step up, and will net pricing improve?
qa_highlights.answer: EV run rate is about 9,000 a month and expected to rise above 10,000 from May; demand is strong but supply constrained. Long-term EV cost trends are deflationary versus inflationary ICE costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Range Rover EV launch timing and pre-bookings?
qa_highlights.answer: Range Rover Electric is coming soon as the first JLR EV launch, with three reveals in H2 CY26. There are no firm pre-bookings, but about 78,000 expressions of interest.

qa_highlights.question: How are geopolitics and fuel prices affecting EV demand and investment plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Middle East war does not change launch timelines or investment plans, but JLR will need to keep ICE, PHEV, MHEV and BEV offerings in parallel for longer than planned.

qa_highlights.question: How is JLR planning to reduce its breakeven volume to 300,000?
qa_highlights.answer: The GBP 1.7 billion plan covers end-to-end procurement (now a separate Board-level vertical), warranty cost reduction and IT/digital productivity; benefits to start from H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected FY27 industry growth and TMPV's supply situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry growth expected at about 10%, with high double-digit H1. Management said FY27 is a supply challenge rather than demand, with two new nameplates and four facelifts each for ICE and EV planned.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a prior-period item in Q4 PLI accrual?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, about Rs 90 Cr related to Q3 that was certified in Q4; excluding it, Q4 PLI would be about Rs 380 Cr against Rs 471 Cr reported.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (aluminium, copper, petrochemical-linked inputs) of 5-6% of revenue with limited pass-through so far; margin depends on further price actions and cost savings.
Middle East conflict: Q1 FY27 demand hit in JLR's 6% Middle East mix and potential component or freight disruption, though no shortages seen yet.
Sierra and EV supply ramp is dependent on casting suppliers and new capacity; EV volumes are constrained despite strong demand.
JLR warranty cost increases (notably the US) and rising VME (7% vs 5%) continue to pressure margins.
Sterling strength against the dollar and tariffs weigh on JLR cash flow; FY26 cash flow was impacted by lower payables.
China luxury tax and the Chinese OEM push in Europe and the UK pose competitive risks for JLR.
key_quotes: So as expected, we did recover strongly in Q4.
Having said that, and delivered what we promised in Q4, it is accepted that our full year financial performance is far from what we had intended when we started the year.
The issue is supply. It will completely depend on ramping up, how fast we are able to ramp up the volumes.
So, given this new world order in supply and demand side of our business, what's our response?
Demand for the moment is slightly a secondary concern.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India demand and the H2 rebound, with management stating demand is strong and the constraint is supply. Cautious and candid on JLR, admitting full-year performance was far from intended and calling for corrective action, and deferring FY27 guidance to the June investor days.

adds.what: Sierra.ev launch (new EV model; supply constrained by casting suppliers, production to cross 10,000 units/month)
EV production ramp beyond 10,000 units/month from May 2026 (about 10% increase from May)

growth.why: Management expects India industry growth of about 10% in FY27 (high double digits in H1, moderating in H2) and aims for industry-beating TMPV growth, backed by EV ramp beyond 10,000/month, Sierra.ev launch next quarter, and 70-100% export growth target; no specific new plant capacity or order numbers were given, so backing is partial.
